overview: After 2...exf4 White plays 3.Ne2 to recapture on f4 with the knight, keeping the pawn structure healthy and avoiding ...Qh4+ and ...g5 lines. Black has several options such as 3...d5, 3...Nf6 or 3...g5; if Black holds the f4 pawn the gambit is still on. It is a rare, quiet-ish way into the King's Gambit.

white_ideas.idea: Retake f4 with the knight, then play d4 and Nbc3
Play d4 and develop with Nf4/Nbc3 and Bc4 or Bf4

black_ideas.idea: Hold f4 with ...g5 or play ...d5 to open the centre

typical_structures.structure: Open King's Gambit centre with Black pawn on f4

character.notes: The King's Gambit family gives open, double-edged positions even in this quiet version.

gambit.notes: Black takes f4 and White does not yet regain it; Black can hold it with ...g5.

soundness.notes: Rare and probably less accurate than the main lines, but not refuted.

structure.notes: Open lines after d4 and the exchange of e-pawns.

approach.notes: A rare sideline of the King's Gambit.

character.reason: King's Gambit positions are usually open and double-edged even when White plays Ne2.

gambit.reason: Black has the f4 pawn and can keep it with ...g5 or ...d5.

soundness.reason: A slightly slow but playable version of the King's Gambit.

structure.reason: The f-pawn and e-pawn exchanges open the centre.

approach.reason: A rare sideline; strong players pick other third moves.

level.reason: Few forcing lines to memorise, but it needs sound judgement.

plans.reason: White aims to regain the pawn with Nxf4 and build the centre.
